sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module setup
sections.what: Loads the path helper, the type labels and the PowerPoint reader.
sections.why: Needed to open proposals and work with file names.

sections.name: SemanticApproachDetector (part 1)
sections.title: Creating the detector and starting the search
sections.what: Stores the RAG engine. For a proposal file it prints progress, sets up five plain-language questions about approach content, opens the proposal, and runs each question through the search limited to proposals.
sections.why: Likely reason: descriptive questions match slides by meaning rather than by exact keywords.
sections.watch_out: The loaded presentation is not used in the visible part of this method, so a bad file fails at opening.

sections.name: SemanticApproachDetector (part 2)
sections.title: Turning search hits into slide scores
sections.what: Reads each search hit, finds the slide number written in its text, and averages the match scores for each slide. It ranks the slides from best to worst match and keeps those under a set cutoff, always keeping at least ten.
sections.why: Likely reason: the search returns text chunks rather than slides, so the slide number is recovered from text markers to map each hit back to a slide.
sections.watch_out: The code treats a lower score as more relevant, the 0.5 cutoff is a guess the code itself flags for adjustment, and the bare except silently skips any hit it cannot parse.

sections.name: SemanticApproachDetector (part 3)
sections.title: Collecting text from chosen slides
sections.what: For each chosen slide, gathers all of its text into one block and stores it with its relevance score. It returns the chosen slide numbers, their text, and the total slide count.
sections.why: Likely reason: the caller needs both the slide numbers and the words on them to show or check the result. No other reason is stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Slide numbers are counted from zero internally, while the verification display adds one, so mixing them up points at the wrong slide.

sections.name: detect_approach_slides_semantically
sections.title: Convenience entry point for detection
sections.what: Runs the whole approach-slide detection for one proposal in a single call. When verbose, it also prints a list of found slides so a person can check it, then returns the results.
sections.why: Likely reason: it hides the setup steps so other code can run detection with one function call.
sections.watch_out: It needs a RAG engine that has already indexed the documents, otherwise the search returns nothing useful.

summary: Finds which slides in one proposal are approach slides by asking the RAG database which parts of that proposal match approach-related questions. Only the start of the detector was visible in the packet.
purpose: Locate approach slides by meaning rather than by keywords.
why: The module docstring says it replaces keyword matching with semantic search.
how: Hold five plain-language questions about timelines, governance, modules, workstreams and methodology. Run each question through the search limited to proposals, keep only results from the named proposal file, then score the slides. Only the search step is visible.
inputs: A RAG engine object and the path to a proposal PowerPoint file.
outputs: A dictionary with approach slide numbers and their content, according to the method's docstring. The final output is not visible in the packet.
risks: The file name filter is a substring test, so a file whose name is contained in another file's name can match the wrong results. The loaded presentation is not used in the visible part.
debug: Turn on verbose to see each question and its results. If no slides come back, check that the proposal is indexed under its exact file name.
